market_laws.title: Resting size change decomposes into execution and cancellation
market_laws.statement: For a price level between two adjacent book snapshots: size_next = size_prev - traded_at_price - cancelled + added. Therefore net_passive_change = added - cancelled = size_next - size_prev + traded_at_price. A level that shrinks was either traded through or cancelled, and no sequence of book snapshots alone can tell which.
market_laws.condition: any price level observed in two adjacent order-book snapshots, with the aggressor-classified trade tape covering the interval between them
market_laws.mechanism_claim: Accounting identity of a limit order book price level. Every unit leaving a level is either executed against an aggressor or withdrawn by its owner; every unit arriving is a new passive order. It is true by construction and cannot decay.
market_laws.temporal_stability: permanent by construction; unaffected by regime, venue or sample
market_laws.review_criterion: Not reviewable as an empirical claim. It would only change if the definition of traded_at_price changed, for example if the tape stopped carrying aggressor side.

tested_variants.variant: identical book delta 100->0 with and without tape volume
tested_variants.result: classifies as PULL vs CONSUMPTION; this is the whole point

market_laws.title: A passive fill at the touch is followed by an adverse move exceeding the captured spread
market_laws.statement: A limit order resting at the touch and filled under a last-in-queue assumption is followed by a mid move against the filled side that is roughly threefold the half-spread it captured. Measured total is -1.07 bps before fees across both sides.
market_laws.condition: limit order placed at best bid or best ask at a book snapshot; filled only when cumulative aggressive volume at that exact price reaches the size displayed there at placement; 60s rest window before cancellation

null_test.reason: exploratory probe; no matched null was constructed

remove_best.reason: single symbol, so remove-best-symbol is undefined

market_laws.mechanism_claim: Adverse selection. A passive order is filled precisely when someone wants to trade against it, which is disproportionately when the filler holds the better short-term view. The liquidity provider is compensated by the spread and taxed by the information in the flow that lifts them.
market_laws.temporal_stability: unknown; measured on one symbol-day. The sign held on both sides and at both horizons, and t is large, but persistence across symbols and regimes is untested.
market_laws.review_criterion: Promote to replicated only after the same measurement across at least 20 symbols with chronological splits, a matched null and remove-best-symbol, all PASS. Mark broken if the sign reverses on any out-of-sample segment.

tested_variants.result: buy -3.32 bps t=-9.01; sell -0.48 bps t=-1.30; combined -1.14 bps

market_laws.source_of_record: maker-fill probe, 2026-08-03, AAVEUSDT 2026-07-15, 8638 placements per side
market_laws.notes: Fees are not deducted. Maker fees would make the total more negative.

market_laws.title: Below roughly five minutes the round-trip cost exceeds one standard deviation of the move
market_laws.statement: Mid-move dispersion scales with horizon while the round-trip cost is a constant, so the share of moves able to pay 11 bps rises from 1.6 percent at 10 seconds to 48.1 percent at 5 minutes. At 60 seconds the 11 bps floor exceeds the 8.6 bps standard deviation of the move, which closes an unfiltered taker route at that horizon regardless of signal quality.
market_laws.condition: mid-to-mid move measured on the recorded book, against the frozen 11 bps round-trip taker cost

null_test.reason: a dispersion measurement has no directional null; the relevant check is replication across symbols

market_laws.mechanism_claim: Variance of a price process grows with elapsed time while a fee and spread charge does not. The ratio of achievable move to fixed cost therefore improves monotonically with horizon, which sets a floor on the shortest tradeable horizon for a given cost structure.
market_laws.temporal_stability: the monotone shape is structural; the specific crossover horizon is symbol and volatility dependent and will move with regime
market_laws.review_criterion: Replicate the crossover horizon across at least 20 symbols and two volatility regimes. The 1h row rests on n=23 and must not be quoted as established.

tested_variants.result: sd 3.6 bps, 1.6 percent beyond cost, n=8637
sd 57.6 bps, 95.7 percent, n=23 — too few, reported but not established
insufficient samples in one symbol-day; not reported

market_laws.notes: t_stat and the interval are zero-width because this is a dispersion table rather than a directional effect; the meaningful uncertainty is the per-horizon n.

market_laws.title: States where aggressive flow and depth change agree are followed by adverse outcomes
market_laws.statement: When aggressive flow over an interval runs against an intended direction AND depth on the side that direction relies on falls over the same interval, the next 60 seconds are systematically adverse to that direction. Such states carry a mean forward move of -0.620 bps against a near-zero +0.095 bps in all other states, a separation of +0.715 bps.
market_laws.condition: for an intended long: aggressive sell notional exceeds aggressive buy notional in the interval between two adjacent book snapshots, and bid-side depth fell over the same interval; exact mirror for an intended short. Both intents evaluated at every snapshot, never a selected subset.

null_test.detail: random guard vetoing at the identical 13.3 percent rate: control centre 0.000 bps, sd 0.036, observed +0.715, p=0.000 two-sided. Roughly twenty standard deviations above the control.

oos.detail: positive in both out-of-sample segments: holdout +0.700 (t=14.8), forward +0.737 (t=13.9)

market_laws.mechanism_claim: Aggressive flow consuming one side of the book while that side is not replenishing is a joint signature of informed liquidity demand and liquidity withdrawal. An entry taken into that state is stepping in front of flow that is still arriving against a book that is thinning, so the immediate expected move is adverse. The measured object is the cost of poor entry timing, not a directional forecast.
market_laws.temporal_stability: Stable across all four chronological splits over 26 days and 10 symbols, and across both horizons. Persistence beyond this archive span, across venues, and across volatility regimes is untested.
market_laws.review_criterion: Promote to replicated only on a SECOND, non-overlapping archive span of at least 10 days per out-of-sample segment. All three checks already PASS, but every split here comes from one 26-day archive, so this is one measurement rather than an independent replication. Mark broken if the ALLOW mean turns materially positive, which would mean the predicate is picking direction rather than suppressing bad states.

market_laws.title: Perp-spot basis dispersion on liquid symbols is an order of magnitude below the two-leg cost floor
market_laws.statement: On liquid Bybit perpetuals the perp-spot basis is confined to a band far narrower than the 22 bps two-leg round trip. Basis standard deviation is 1.4-1.7 bps on XRP, BTC, SOL and ETH, so reaching the cost floor requires 13-15 standard deviations. Across the six most liquid symbols the basis exceeded 22 bps in 0.016 percent of 158,826 observations. Dispersion rises monotonically with illiquidity: only the two microcaps in the sample, TAC and VANRY, cross the floor with any regularity, at 41 and 57 percent. A separate and less certain observation is that the mean basis is negative on 17 of 18 symbols at roughly -5 to -8 bps; see notes, this may not be a market fact.
market_laws.condition: 15-minute aligned perp and spot closes for the 18 Bybit symbols carrying both legs in axisA; 2025-07-01 to 2026-07-10; basis defined as 1e4*(perp-spot)/spot
market_laws.horizon: 15m observation interval; mean-reversion half-life measured at 0.09-1.42h, median 0.20h
market_laws.transform_version: axisA/aligned.json row order [ts, PERP, SPOT, funding], verified against backfill_axisA.mjs:19; exploratory descriptive measurement 2026-08-03

null_test.reason: descriptive dispersion measurement; no trading rule was formed, so there is no rule to match a null against

remove_best.reason: the claim is per-symbol and reported per-symbol, so there is no pooled contribution for a best symbol to dominate

market_laws.mechanism_claim: Arbitrage between a perpetual and its spot leg is cheap and heavily contested on liquid symbols, so the basis is compressed to a band narrower than the cost of crossing it. The compression is itself the evidence of competition: dispersion scales inversely with liquidity, and only where the arbitrage is expensive or impossible does the basis widen past the floor.
market_laws.temporal_stability: Measured over 375 continuous days spanning several regimes. The ordering of symbols by dispersion was stable; no sub-period was examined separately.
market_laws.review_criterion: Promote to replicated only after (a) the alignment artifact in the notes is excluded, and (b) the dispersion result is reproduced on an independently constructed perp-spot join. Mark broken if any liquid symbol shows a sustained period with more than 1 percent of observations beyond 22 bps.

market_laws.source_of_record: exploratory descriptive measurement over axisA/aligned.json, 534,051 rows, 18 symbols, 375 days
market_laws.notes: UNRESOLVED, recorded deliberately. The persistent negative mean of -5 to -8 bps may be an artifact of our own join rather than a property of the market. Two candidate explanations were considered. A timing lag between the spot and perp bar is the obvious one, but it is weakened by the evidence: a lag artifact scales with volatility, yet the mean sits in a narrow -5 to -8 band while the standard deviation varies twentyfold across symbols. A constant definitional offset -- perp mark price against spot last trade, or an index versus a venue price -- fits the observed near-constancy better. Neither was tested. The decision-relevant part of this law is the DISPERSION, which is robust to any additive offset: shifting every observation by 8 bps cannot move BTC from 13.7 sigma to within reach of the floor. The mean is recorded for completeness and must not be cited as evidence of backwardation until the review criterion is met. The t-statistic is reported with autocorrelation adjustment but cannot distinguish a real effect from a systematic offset, and so carries no weight on this question.

data_constraints.title: Historical funding archive carries settlement time, not publication time
data_constraints.statement: The historical funding archive contains a settlement timestamp but no publication or ingest timestamp; therefore using a value for a decision before settlement creates unprovable causality and a potential look-ahead.
data_constraints.scope_note: Applies to this dataset specifically. It is not a claim about historical funding archives in general, nor about any future forward-recorded funding series.
evidence: Schema carries exactly one time field per record: ts, alongside by_r, by_p, bi_r, bi_p, ok_r, ok_p. No publication field, no predicted-rate field, no ingest field.
All 691 BTCUSDT timestamps fall exactly on 00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC, with zero off-schedule records. That is the Bybit funding settlement grid.

All ten per-symbol files were written between 2026-07-11T11:46:59Z and 11:47:06Z, one backfill batch, covering values from 2025-06-01 onward. Ingest time is therefore later than every historical decision time.
Second-leg fields are absent or empty: ok_p is 0 percent populated across every symbol, and there is no spot price, borrow rate, basis, or bid/ask on either leg.
Coverage is 691 of roughly 1215 expected 8-hour intervals over 405 days, with gaps up to 112 hours.
data_constraints.consequence: Causal funding carry cannot be evaluated on this dataset. The current Carry implementation is closed. This cannot be repaired by backfill, because the predicted funding rate is a live-only observable and is not retrievable retrospectively.
data_constraints.review_criterion: Only on a new source carrying publication_ts, or our own forward-recorded series carrying ingest_ts captured at observation time. Indirect reconstruction of the publication moment is explicitly not an acceptable route.

data_constraints.title: The 11 bps research cost floor is fees only and understates realised taker cost by roughly 5 bps
data_constraints.statement: Every hypothesis in this programme was evaluated against an 11 bps single-leg round trip, hardcoded independently in six engines with no derivation. That figure contains two taker fee legs and nothing else. The repository documents a realistic all-in Bybit VIP0 round trip of 0.160 percent, which is 16 bps, and a live operating rule that permits a taker entry only above 0.13 percent per round trip, which is 13 bps. Both exceed the research constant. The gap reconciles to the execution components the constant omits: measured taker slippage of 4.46 bps and spread of 1.1 bps over 29 live round trips.
data_constraints.scope_note: Applies to the cost floor used in research engines, not to live PnL accounting, which is reconciled to the cent against real fills and is unaffected.
evidence: cost_bps_roundtrip: 11 appears in ah019:64, ah041:35, ah046:29, ah048:36, and as cost_bps_both_legs: 22 in simple_pairs:34 and market_neutral_funding_carry:38, with no shared definition and no source.
BOTALIN_RESEARCH_SUMMARY_FOR_EXTERNAL_AI_2026-07-18.md:276 -- conservative taker model 0.250 RT was harsher than the real Bybit VIP0 of about 0.160 RT.
docs/BOTALIN_HANDOFF_2026-07-13_REV6.md:17 -- forensics over 29 valid round trips: taker slip +4.46 bps, spread 1.1 bps, maker slip -1.1 bps, adverse under 2 bps, reconciled to the cent.
Same line records the adopted live rule: taker only when expected edge exceeds 0.13 percent per round trip.
Whether the 1.1 bps spread is already contained inside the 4.46 bps slippage depends on the unrecorded reference price, so the audit adopts the reconciled 16 bps rather than publishing a new sum.
data_constraints.consequence: Re-evaluation of all six closed results at 13 and 16 bps deepens every closure and reopens none; the closest approach, the AH-048 sweep continuation at 900s, falls from 81 percent of the floor to 69 and then 56 percent. The existing record therefore stands without re-running. Future tasks must use 16 bps single-leg and 32 bps two-leg, retaining 11/22 only as an optimistic bound for comparison against the historical record. The maker escape route does not open this: the spread is narrower than the maker fee on most liquid symbols, and our own maker-fill probe measured -1.07 bps before fees at t=-9.07.
data_constraints.review_criterion: Resolved only by committing a versioned fee schedule carrying venue, tier, taker rate, maker rate and effective_from, and by deriving the floor from it in one shared module rather than six independent constants. A change of fee tier or venue reopens this record rather than closing it.
data_constraints.source_of_record: cost model audit over committed artifacts and documents, 2026-08-04
